boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Iowa State rituals, legends, recurring celebrations, and pieces of campus lore—from silent lake laps to midnight Campanile kisses.

cards.title: Become an Iowa Stater at Midnight
cards.subtitle: The midnight-kiss tradition beneath the Campanile
cards.notes: Visit the Campanile at midnight with a consenting partner, listen for the bells, and keep the central-campus setting quiet and respectful.
cards.short_summary: Campus tradition says a student officially becomes an Iowa Stater after a midnight kiss beneath the Campanile.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State says a student officially becomes an Iowa Stater when kissed beneath the Campanile at the stroke of midnight.
cards.access_notes: The ritual occurs beneath the Campanile on central campus at midnight; participation should always be consensual.

cards.title: Circle Lake LaVerne Three Times in Silence
cards.subtitle: A relationship legend measured in quiet laps
cards.notes: Walk three silent laps with your beloved on the established shoreline route, allowing extra time for construction or temporary path closures.
cards.short_summary: Three silent circuits of Lake LaVerne supposedly seal a couple’s shared destiny.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State documents the tradition that beloveds who silently walk around Lake LaVerne three times are destined to remain together.
cards.access_notes: Use established paths around Lake LaVerne and observe any posted detours associated with shoreline work.

cards.title: Greet the Swans Who Inherit Their Names
cards.subtitle: Every resident pair continues a naming custom from 1935
cards.notes: Look for Lancelot and Elaine from the lakeside path, use a zoom lens for photographs, and do not approach, touch, or feed the swans.
cards.short_summary: Successive resident swans at Lake LaVerne retain the storybook names Lancelot and Elaine.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State says Lake LaVerne has housed swans named Lancelot and Elaine since 1935 and identifies the current pair as two females.
cards.access_notes: The swans may be viewed from campus paths around Lake LaVerne; visitors should not feed or handle them.

cards.title: Sidestep the Zodiac Before Your Next Exam
cards.subtitle: A bronze floor relief with an academic curse
cards.notes: Enter Gold Star Hall, locate the bronze Zodiac in the floor, and follow generations of cautious Cyclones by walking around its perimeter.
cards.short_summary: Students avoid the Memorial Union’s Zodiac because stepping on it supposedly dooms their next exam.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State says students, staff, faculty, and alumni avoid stepping on the Zodiac to escape the superstition that they will flunk their next exam.
cards.access_notes: The Zodiac is inside Gold Star Hall at the Memorial Union and is available only while the building is open.

cards.entity_name: Fountain of the Four Seasons Coin Cure
cards.title: Reverse the Zodiac Curse with a Coin
cards.subtitle: The traditional remedy for an unlucky step
cards.notes: Learn the coin-cure story beside the fountain, but follow the Memorial Union’s current preservation request and keep objects out of the water.
cards.short_summary: Campus lore prescribes a fountain coin for an accidental Zodiac step, although preservation guidance now discourages tossing objects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Union documents throwing a coin into the Fountain of the Four Seasons as the traditional Zodiac-curse cure while asking visitors not to place objects in the fountain.
cards.access_notes: Observe the fountain from the surrounding plaza and honor current preservation guidance by keeping people and objects out.

cards.title: Hear the Fight Song Become a Competition
cards.subtitle: Homecoming skits built from chants, cheers, and Cyclone spirit
cards.notes: Consult the annual Homecoming calendar for a public round, expect high-volume performances, and follow the posted audience and venue directions.
cards.short_summary: Student teams turn chants, cheers, and the fight song into Iowa State’s long-running Homecoming performance contest.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State’s official 2025 events calendar listed Yell Like Hell rounds and said the skits often use chants and cheers and must include the Iowa State fight song.
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled Homecoming competition; dates, venues, eligibility, and public access are set annually.

cards.title: Watch Cyclone Stories Rise from Front Lawns
cards.subtitle: Hand-built sets and repeating skits in the Greek neighborhood
cards.notes: Use the current Homecoming route, remain on designated viewing paths, and watch the repeating skits without entering sets or active work areas.
cards.short_summary: Participating organizations construct elaborate lawn sets and perform short Homecoming skits beside them.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State’s 2025 events calendar described lawn displays in participating Greek-neighborhood yards, with teams performing skits on hand-built sets.
cards.access_notes: Display locations and viewing times change each Homecoming; use the annual event listing and neighborhood signs.

cards.title: Count Down to a Campus-Wide Midnight Kiss
cards.subtitle: Homecoming’s large-scale version of Campaniling
cards.notes: Arrive early for the central-campus program, choose whether to participate or simply watch, and treat every kiss as an opt-in interaction.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming scales Campaniling into a midnight gathering accompanied by the bells and fireworks.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State’s 2025 listing scheduled free Mass Campaniling on central campus and described the traditional midnight kiss beneath the Campanile during fireworks.
cards.access_notes: The verified 2025 event ran from 10 p.m. to midnight on central campus; future dates require the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Celebrate the Mascot Born at Homecoming
cards.subtitle: A cardinal created because a cyclone resisted costuming
cards.notes: Find Cy at an official campus appearance and compare the modern mascot with the archival image documenting his 1954 Homecoming debut.
cards.short_summary: Iowa State treats Homecoming 1954 as the birth of Cy, the cardinal chosen to embody an otherwise uncostumable cyclone.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State says Cy was born in 1954 and explains that a cardinal was selected because a cyclone was difficult to depict in costume.
cards.access_notes: Cy’s appearances vary by event; check the organizer’s current listing for location, admission, and photography rules.

cards.title: Watch the Giant Spruce Light Up for WinterFest
cards.subtitle: Carillon music and a seasonal countdown on central campus
cards.notes: Check the WinterFest schedule, dress for an outdoor December gathering, and arrive before the countdown for a clear view from central campus.
cards.short_summary: A towering central-campus spruce becomes the focus of Iowa State’s recurring WinterFest lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State reported that the central-campus holiday tree would be illuminated during a 6 p.m. WinterFest ceremony on December 5, 2025.
cards.access_notes: This outdoor ceremony is seasonal; confirm the current WinterFest date, weather plans, and central-campus gathering point.
